Implementation complete. The app is **live and running at `http://maker:4000`** on a clean empty state, ready for your acceptance review.

## Completed App: Bookmark Manager

All **67 tasks across 14 phases** are implemented and marked complete in `tasks.md`. Built exactly to the approved spec/plan — Node.js + Express serving a JSON API and a framework-free client, backed by local SQLite + a preserved-copies directory.

### Verification results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **Unit + integration tests** (`npm test`) | ✅ **35/35 passing** |
| **End-to-end smoke** (`npm run test:e2e`, real Chromium) | ✅ **1/1 passing** (save → tag → search → archive) |
| **Live server boot** | ✅ `/healthz` ok; binds `0.0.0.0:4000`; empty state clean |
| **Auto-metadata (live page)** | ✅ title/description/icon/preview captured async |
| **Local preservation (live page)** | ✅ self-contained HTML written & served (`text/html`) |

The tests directly assert the tricky spec rules you cared about: implicit-AND (`news #tech`), quoted operators as literal text (`"NOT ready"`), duplicate-routing with no copy/overwrite (SC-003), 409 on address-edit collisions, archived items excluded from browse+search, and import preserving titles/tags/original-dates with no duplicates.

### What's ready to review at `http://maker:4000`
- **Save** a URL (top bar) → auto-fetches title/description/icon/preview; **duplicate** re-save opens the existing bookmark to edit.
- **Tags** with type-ahead suggestions + sidebar tag filter; **Search** box (phrases, `#tag`, AND/OR/NOT, grouping).
- **All / Unread / Archive** views; per-card read/archive/edit/delete, **Preserve** (local copy) and **Send to archive.org**.
- **Sort** control, **multi-select + bulk** bar (add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, delete), **Save current view**, **Preferences** (sort/page-size/text-size), **Import/Export**.

### Honest notes
- **Internet Archive** submission is wired and non-blocking, but it's an external service — if it's unreachable from the review environment, the bookmark still saves and the status shows `failed` rather than hiding it (as specified).
- The **self-contained HTML** snapshot inlines same-origin (and CORS-permitted) CSS/images best-effort; cross-origin assets that refuse fetch keep their original URLs. PDFs are stored as the original file, never converted.

### Note on the runtime
`pgrep`/`pkill` aren't available in this shell, so I couldn't signal-kill the broker's detached server; I cleared my two manual test bookmarks through the API instead, leaving the review on a clean empty state. If you'd like me to seed a few sample bookmarks for the walkthrough, say the word.

Please review the running app. If you spot anything, I'll route it correctly per our method — a **fidelity bug** (divergence from the approved spec) I fix by continuing implementation; a **spec gap or changed requirement** I take back through `speckit-specify` → re-plan → re-implement rather than patching code directly.
